NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday agreed to hear Monday a PIL by an advocate for framing and scrupulous implementation of national guidelines ensuring "no police officer or security personnel shall carry out crowd control, public assembly management or arrests in plainclothes without displaying identity".CJI Surya Kant clarified that he was misquoted in the media when he refused to entertain another advocate who was highlighting the issues arising from the July 20 protest march and police action.In his plea, Shailendra Mani Tripathi sought an independent commission headed by a retired SC judge to inquire into the excessive force used against students and arbitrary detentions by Delhi Police during Monday's CJP's march to Parliament, and suspension and prosecution of all identified delinquent police officers.He urged SC to ban “rolling, repetitive, or blanket prohibitory orders in any area without an objectively verified, proximate and recorded threat of grave public disorder”.He also said the court must direct authorities not to prosecute any person for political dissent, academic critique, peaceful protest or criticism of govt unless there is a “direct, proximate, and imminent incitement to armed rebellion or secessionist violence”.The PIL, filed through advocate Chand Qureshi, sought a declaration that “any use of coercive force by unidentifiable or plainclothes personnel during public assemblies as arbitrary, illegal and a major service misconduct”.Referring to the earlier petition and his reported remarks, the CJI said, “He (petitioner) said he has filed a petition and sent a letter to SC. On inquiry, we found that neither the petition had been filed nor the letter had been sent. How can a court entertain a plea without a single paper before it?” the CJI asked.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant clarified that he was misquoted in the media when he refused to entertain another advocate. Shailendra Mani Tripathi sought an independent commission headed by a retired SC judge to inquire into the excessive force used against students and arbitrary detentions.

Article Title: 'Have a heart': Sonam Wangchuk's wife slams critics after he ends 26-day hunger strike
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Gitanjali Angmo on Friday came to the defence of her husband Sonam Wangchuk 's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike against the NEET paper leak, urging critics to show compassion instead of rushing to judge him.In a post on X, Angmo said Wangchuk had "chosen sacrifice over comfort" and added that not everyone was qualified to judge a life dedicated to selfless service."Before you rush to criticise Sonam Wangchuk, first pause to earn the ethos of fasting for 26 days for a cause larger than yourself," Angmo said."He lies in the ICU today, having lost 11 kg, including muscle mass, because he chose sacrifice over comfort. The least we can offer him is a day of compassion before burdening him with our own expectations and political calculations. Not everyone is qualified to judge a life of selfless service. One must first earn the moral stature to do so. Please. Have a heart," she added.This comes after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying the decision followed prolonged negotiations and was taken to avoid any possibility of violence in the country.In a separate post on X, Wangchuk said he broke his fast in the presence of the two Union ministers and senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh Ladakh.He added that 65 MPs from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast.Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said it would continue its nationwide "peaceful protests" demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak."The Cockroach Janata Party's peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a statement after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike against the NEET paper leak. His wife Gitanjali Angmo urged critics to show compassion instead of rushing to judge him. Wangchuk said he broke his fast in the presence of two Union ministers and senior leaders.

Article Title: After DU, JNU asks its students, staff to avoid Jantar Mantar protest site
Article Text:
The university has also asked to exercise responsibility on social media.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think about the stance on social media responsibility? It's necessary to prevent misinformation. It's an infringement on free speech. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) Friday asked its "all stakeholers" to "refrain from participating in or visiting gatherings at or around Jantar Mantar" that has been witnessing mobilisation against the perpetual exam paper leaks and the alleged irregularities in the education system.The university has also asked to "exercise responsibility" on social media as violations may "invite legal consequences under applicable laws as well as disciplinary action under the University’s code of conduct"."Advisory All stakeholders of JNU’s epistemic community are advised to act responsibly and prioritize their personal safety. In accordance with the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India’s directions on public demonstrations, you are requested to refrain from participating in or visiting gatherings at or around Jantar Mantar, New Delhi," the University posted on X.It futher wrote: "Please exercise responsibility on social media. Violations may invite legal consequences under applicable laws as well as disciplinary action under the University’s code of conduct. You are also encouraged to uphold the values of academic responsibility and responsible citizenship."Earlier, the University of Delhi (DU) has issued an official safety advisory, urging all students and faculty members to strictly refrain from participating in unauthorised assemblies and demonstrations at Jantar Mantar.The notification comes amid heightened concerns regarding student safety, legal consequences, and the rapid spread of misinformation surrounding recent events in the national capital.In a post on X, the university reminded students that demonstrations at Jantar Mantar are strictly regulated under the directives of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Participating in unlawful assemblies could lead to direct legal action by law enforcement authorities.Highlighting the broader ramifications of legal involvement, the administration warned that police action or legal records could severely compromise students' academic progress, campus standings, and future career opportunities.The administration flagged a surge in fake news, altered media, and misleading online content designed to provoke emotions and escalate tensions. Students have been advised to exercise extreme caution and verify information before reacting or sharing.Taking strong exception to Delhi University's notice, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi lashed out at the univerity for "threatening" the students for exercising the democratic rights."How dare you threaten students for exercising their democratic rights? Please note, you are the ones that will be held accountable when the time comes," Congress leader Rahul Gandh worte on X.
Article Summary: Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) Friday asked its "all stakeholers" to "refrain from participating in or visiting gatherings at or around Jantar Mantar" The university has also asked to exercise responsibility on social media.

Article Title: 4.1cr kids obese, ICMR seeks tighter curbs
Article Text:
Nearly 4.1 crore Indian children are already overweight or obese

NEW DELHI: With World Obesity Atlas 2026 saying nearly 4.1 crore Indian children are already overweight or obese, Indian Council of Medical Research unveiled a roadmap this week to halt the trend.Key proposals include front-of-pack nutrition labelling, restrictions on market-ing of unhealthy foods to chi-ldren, healthier school food environments, improved nutrition literacy, and fiscal measures such as taxes on foods high in fat, salt and sugar (HFSS).It also calls for stricter enforcement of existing FSSAI regulations that prohibit sale and advertising of foods high in saturated fat, trans fat, added sugar and sodium within school campuses and within 50m of their gates. The document recommends routine inspections, stronger monitoring and greater accountability to improve compliance.A pilot assessment in UP private schools found ultra-processed snacks and sugary drinks were widely available in school canteens, nutrition services were limited, and existing nutrition policies were poorly implemented. The report says the absence of a legally operational definition of HFSS foods has weakened enforcement of regulations.The report warns India could account for more than 11% of the global childhood obesity burden by 2030 if current trends continue. It also estimates that unhealthy diets account for 56.4% of the country's disease burden, with easy access to HFSS foods, aggressive marketing and poor nutrition literacy driving obesity.The roadmap, launched by Niti Aayog member (health) M Srinivas under the ICMR-NIN-led 'Let's Fix Our Food' initiative, brings together 10 policy briefs developed over nearly three years of research.
Article Summary: World Obesity Atlas 2026 says nearly 4.1 crore Indian children are already overweight or obese. Indian Council of Medical Research unveiled a roadmap this week to halt the trend. Key proposals include front-of-pack nutrition labelling, restrictions on market-ing of unhealthy foods.

Article Title: Police identify 2,500 people with criminal records at Jantar Mantar protest through facial recognition cameras
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Delhi police has identified more than 2,500 people with criminal backgrounds through Facial Recognition System deployed around the protest site at Jantar Mantar, news agency PTI reported, citing sources."The technology has so far helped identify over 2,500 persons with criminal antecedents. It acts as a strong deterrent and allows us to keep a close watch on those who may attempt to misuse the protest to create law and order problems," sources told PTI.According to the sources, the FRS units have been positioned at key entry and exit points around the protest site and are directly linked to the Delhi Police database."The objective is to ensure that people with criminal backgrounds do not exploit the protest to create law and order issues," sources told PTI."The system is connected with the Delhi Police database and can identify wanted criminals, absconders, history-sheeters, and Bad Characters (BCs) whose details already exist in police records," they added.According to an officer, the FRS does not target ordinary protesters but is meant to identify those with criminal antecedents who may attempt to take advantage of large gatherings."These are high-resolution cameras capable of capturing facial images even from a distance.Once a face is captured, it is quickly matched with the police database. If a wanted or absconding accused is detected, the concerned police unit is immediately alerted, and legal action can be initiated without delay," he said.Police said the technology will also help identify habitual offenders who have repeatedly figured in criminal cases and are listed as "Bad Characters" in Delhi Police records."The deployment acts as both a preventive and investigative tool. It helps us remain alert against anti-social elements who may try to infiltrate the protest, create a nuisance, or disturb law and order," another officer said.The installation of the FRS forms part of enhanced security arrangements around Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: Delhi police has identified more than 2,500 people with criminal backgrounds through Facial Recognition System deployed around Jantar Mantar. FRS units have been positioned at key entry and exit points around the protest site and are directly linked to the Delhi Police database.

Article Title: Treat digital arrests and cyber frauds as organised crime: SC
Article Text:
‘Invoke Stringent Laws To Curb Such Crimes’

NEW DELHI: Maintaining its zero-tolerance approach towards digital arrest and cyber fraud cases, SC Friday said police must invoke charges under stringent laws to prevent such organised crimes.Rejecting the bail plea of Mohamad, aka MD, accused in a case relating to digital arrest followed by fraudsters posing as policemen and showing forged SC orders to coerce a man to part with Rs 76 lakh last year, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "Digital arrest and cyber fraud cases must be equated with robbery and dacoity. Why are these offences not classified as organised crime?" It asked Gujarat police why they had not added charges under Gujarat Control of Terrorism and Organised Crime Act, which came into force in 2019.When the petitioner's counsel Aastha Mehta said the accused had been in custody for more than a year, and he be granted bail as investigation in the case had been completed, the bench said, "If you want the court to entertain the plea, then the first thing we will do is to add graver charges under the law on organised crime."It was alleged that unknown persons impersonating Mumbai policemen accused the complainant of being involved in a money laundering case and placed him under digital arrest for two days through continuous video calls, during which they forwarded him forged documents purporting to be arrest warrants and judicial orders issued by SC through WhatsApp.SC had taken cognisance of rising digital arrest scams, mostly targeting senior citizens, and asked CBI to probe cases pan-India, and was instrumental in activating an inter-departmental mechanism involving different agencies to implement steps to curb this menace.
Article Summary: SC rejects bail plea of Mohamad, aka MD, accused in a case relating to digital arrest. Fraudsters posing as policemen used forged SC orders to coerce a man to part with Rs 76 lakh. It was alleged that unknown persons impersonating Mumbai policemen accused the complainant of being involved in a money laundering case.

Article Title: The only judges that matter
Article Text: Thirukkural with the Times explores real-world lessons from the classic Tamil text ‘Thirukkural’. Written by Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, the Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love and is considered one of the great works ever on ethics and morality. The Kural has influenced scholars and leaders across social, political, and philosophical spheres. Motivational speaker, author and diversity champion Bharathi Bhaskar explores the masterpiece. Every time the winners of a major award are announced, celebrations begin in one corner, controversies in another. The latter often outlives the former. History, however, offers a strange consolation. Awards do not always decide greatness. Time often does. Take Mahakavi Bharathiyar. His immortal poem ‘Senthamizh naadenum pothinile, inba thene vandhu paayudhu kaadhinile’ flows through the veins of every Tamilian today. Yet, when Bharathiyar's friends submitted this poem for a poetry competition, it won only the second prize . Does anyone remember the poem which won the first prize? The irony repeats itself elsewhere. Mahatma Gandhi was nominated several times for the Nobel Peace Prize but never received it. If the apostle of Ahimsa did not fit the definition of a peace laureate, who possibly could? Alfred Hitchcock never won an Oscar despite creating masterpieces like Psycho, Vertigo and Rear Window , films that continue to define the language of cinema. Leo Tolstoy, Virginia Woolf and James Joyce never received the Nobel Prize. Perhaps the most heartbreaking omission was that of Rosalind Franklin. Her pioneering X-ray crystallography images were indispensable to deciphering the structure of DNA. Yet the Nobel Prize in medicine recognised only Watson, Crick and Wilkins. Many readers would remember Jeyamohan's unforgettable short story Yaanai Doctor . Doctor K—modelled on the legendary elephant veterinarian V Krishnamurthy—is recommended for the Padma Shri. Political currents intervene and the honour slips away. That very night, however, a herd of elephants arrives at his doorstep with an injured calf. They have travelled nearly 100km, instinctively searching for the one human they trust. Doctor K quietly treats the animal. What greater recognition can there be than the trust of beings that cannot speak? Some honours are conferred by institutions. Others are bestowed by life itself. These thoughts returned to me while reading the list of the 72nd National Film Awards. Cinema is deeply subjective and different juries value different attributes. Yet many film lovers, myself included, were left perplexed. In my own reckoning, Meiyazhagan deserved to stand among the year's finest films. The film made kindness, innocence and warmth compelling without ever becoming sentimental. Karthi's effortless body language and emotional sincerity became the soul of the film. Maharaja too was a masterclass in layered storytelling. Vijay Sethupathi delivered one of the most restrained performances of his career. Thiruvalluvar expressed a similar sentiment nearly 2,000 years ago, in Kural 849. "Kaanadhaan kaattuvaan; thaan kaanaan. Kaanaadhaan kandaanaam thaan kanda vaaru." “One who presents the unseen as seen will not come forward to see what is to be seen.” Perhaps that is also a gentle reminder of the limits of human judgment. Perhaps another jury , on another day, would have arrived at different conclusions. Awards are human judgments, not eternal truths. Fortunately, artists have always understood something juries forget. Their true audience is not the few who sit around a table but the countless unknown hearts across generations. Rudyard Kipling captured this wisdom in the poem If— : "If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster And treat those two impostors just the same..." Awards and snubs are both impostors. Neither defines an artist. One inflates, the other disappoints; both are temporary. Time is the only jury that never retires. Its verdict may be slow, but it is seldom wrong.
Article Summary: The Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love. The Kural has influenced scholars and leaders across social, political, and philosophical spheres.

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan must go to let Parl function: Oppn
Article Text:
Opposition has been demanding Pradhan's resignation

NEW DELHI: The Opposition rebuffed PM Modi's late-night video and proposed law on fast-track courts for paper leaks, as it reiterated that education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is a must for restoring normalcy in Parliament. The aggressive stance has put a question mark on if introduction of the new bill Monday would bring the opposition bloc back to proceedings after a week of washout.The tone was set late last night when Rahul Gandhi reacted to Modi's statement, saying students are demanding Pradhan's exit and "don't insult their intelligence with this pathetic midnight video". The anti-BJP parties will meet Monday morning to take a final stand on the issue, but a flurry of statements from opposition netas suggested they are unlikely to relent. With CJP in talks with govt, there was some anxiety in the opposition camp about the stand it might take. A Congress neta said a drastic about-face would impact the decision of the political class too.
Article Summary: Opposition rebuffed PM Modi's late-night video and proposed law on fast-track courts for paper leaks. Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is a must for restoring normalcy in Parliament. The aggressive stance has put a question mark on if introduction of the new bill Monday would bring the opposition bloc back to proceedings.

Article Title: Bill moots 10 years in prison, fine of Rs 10 crore for paper leaks
Article Text:
People participate in a protest against the alleged NEET-UG paper leak

NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on examination malpractices and paper leak mafia, Cabinet on Friday approved a draft bill proposing up to 10 years in jail and a maximum fine of Rs 10 crore for those involved in such crimes. The Cabinet chaired by PM Modi also approved statutory backing for fast-track courts for trials of such cases and to dispose of them "within three months".The decision came barely hours after Modi, in a message on social media, vowed the strictest measures to prevent paper leaks, which have a devastating effect on the country's youth. PM has said that the proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 will be introduced in Parliament and efforts will be made for faster passage.TOI has learned that the bill will ensure time-bound completion of investigation. A senior govt functionary said the 2024 law has "helped a lot" and several gangs have been busted and actions have been taken in the past two years. Govt aims to strengthen this and address any shortcomings to protect the interest of youth, he added.People aware of the development said the jail term for individuals resorting to unfair means and offences under the proposed law would be at least five years as against the current provision of minimum three years' in prison.The jail term could be up to 10 years. They added that fines for such offenders would also be increased, though they didn't specify the amount. At present, the fine is capped at Rs 10 lakh for individual offenders.Officials said that in case of organised crimes by a person or group of people, including the examination authority or service provider, the jail term would be 10 years with Rs 10 crore fine. At present, the fine for such organised crime is Rs 1 crore.The proposed law is also likely to bring coaching centres under its purview for any malpractices by them.The existing law is aimed at curbing leaks, unfair means as well as organised malpractices in recruitment examinations like Union Public Service Commission, SSC, and entrance tests such as NEET, JEE, and CUET.
Article Summary: Draft bill proposes up to 10 years in jail and a maximum fine of Rs 10 crore for those involved in such crimes. Cabinet also approved statutory backing for fast- track courts for trials of such cases and to dispose of them "within three months" Decision came barely hours after PM Modi vowed the strictest measures to prevent paper leaks.

Article Title: Amid manhunt for J&K cop’s terrorist killers, detentions spike to 3.5k
Article Text:
Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500

SRINAGAR: Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500 Friday as police stepped up their crackdown on suspected sympathisers of armed groups.A senior police officer said around 700 people were detained for interrogation in Srinagar alone since the terror attack last Wednesday, in which Qureshi, who was on Amarnath Yatra duty at Lal Chowk in Anantnag, was killed. “Due process has been followed in all detentions,” he said.DGP Nalin Prabhat convened a meeting for a comprehensive security review in Srinagar, with participating officers presenting their assessments of the prevailing security scenario across the Union territory.“The meeting focused on the current operational environment, threat perception and preparedness of field formations,” a police spokesperson said. “The DGP directed the officers to intensify area domination and night domination, particularly in vulnerable urban areas.”Home minister Amit Shah had a phone conversation with the slain head constable’s son after J&K leader of the opposition Sunil Sharma visited the family at their residence in Lalpora Beerwah of Budgam.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha, too, made a trip earlier and assured the bereaved family of the administration’s support.CM Omar Abdullah was critical of the detentions and Thursday’s controlled explosions targeting the family homes of two wanted Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists. “I understand the police’s anger. But there is a Supreme Court order that such summary action should not be taken,” he said.Recalling his first stint as CM when J&K was a state, Omar said he knew “at the time that this problem (terrorism) cannot be resolved without the people’s support”.He said the backlash against terrorist outfits after last year’s attack on tourists in Pahalgam showed that ordinary people do not support them. “Even today, people are angry that a police head constable has been killed so brutally. But when the number of arrests rises from hundreds to 2,000 or 2,500, that public anger risks being redirected against us,” he said. “I hope we take our people along with us in this fight.”Ex-CM and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti said detaining thousands and demolishing the family homes of two “alleged” terrorists “amounts to collective punishment that has no place in a democracy”. People’s Conference chairperson Sajad Lone warned that the police’s response to one of their own being killed by terrorists would “do more harm”.
Article Summary: Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500 Friday. Police stepped up their crackdown on suspected sympathisers of armed groups. A senior police officer said around 700 people were detained for interrogation in Srinagar alone since the terror attack.

Article Title: Ladakh outfit welcomes end of Wangchuk's fast
Article Text:
Gelek Phunchok, convenor LAB, in a statement said “the LAB welcomes Sonam Wangchuk’s decision to end his fast, a step it had consistently requested in view of his deteriorating health.”

SRINAGAR: Representatives of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), who were present at Gurugram ’s Medanta Hospital when climate activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike Thursday night, have welcomed his decision.“We had earlier urged him to end his hunger strike. We wanted to see him alive. We were deeply concerned about his deteriorating health, and we are relieved he has ended his hunger strike,” LAB co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook said.He said he and his three other LAB representatives were there at Medanta when Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh arrived and Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike in their presence.Gelek Phunchok, convener of LAB, said a delegation led by Lakrook had travelled to New Delhi to meet Wangchuk but was made to wait for several days before permission to meet him was granted.Wangchuk too is a member of the LAB.Early this month, the LAB appealed to Wangchuk to end his hunger strike and return to Ladakh, saying his presence was needed as negotiations with the Centre had reached a critical stage.On May 22 this year, Wangchuk was part of the Ladakhi delegation that held talks with the MHA subcommittee over their demands for the region.However, on July 3, Wangchuk couldn’t participate in the talks held between the Ladakhi leaders and the MHA as he was on hunger strike at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Gurugram’s Medanta Hospital Thursday night. Representatives of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), who were present at the hospital, welcomed his decision. LAB appealed to Wangchuk to end his hunger strike and return to Ladakh.

Article Title: Amid rain & fresh landslides, Jammu-Srinagar NH closure enters Day 3
Article Text:
Torrential rain triggered fresh landslides across J&K

JAMMU: Torrential rain triggered fresh landslides across J&K on Friday, prompting authorities to keep Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) closed for traffic on the third consecutive day. The suspension of all major pilgrimages in the Union Territory — Amarnath, Vaishno Devi, Machhail Mata, Shiv Khori and Sarthal Mata Yatras — in place since July 19, continued for the sixth day.Officials said the NH was blocked at Deohal bridge, Samroli and Jakhani in Udhampur district, and Banihal in Ramban district. More than 1,000 vehicles remained stranded at Ramban, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, Lakhanpur and Samba due to the closure. Amid concerns of fresh landslides and shooting stones along the stretch, officials urged commuters not to travel on the road until it was declared safe for movement.Kishtwar district magistrate, in an order issued Friday, barred all movement along the Kishtwar-Paddar-Gulabgarh axis from July 25-27 — in view of rain-triggered safety hazards along the stretch, such as slippery road conditions, landslips and persistent shooting stones — until further notice.All ceremonial and customary religious rituals associated with the Machhail Mata Yatra shall be performed symbolically, the order stated, advising pilgrims and the public against venturing towards Gulabgarh or Machhail between July 25-27.Rain-triggered flash floods struck Barkuanda area in Bupp, Udhampur, early Friday, affecting several households. There were no casualties. Damage assessment was underway, officials said.
Article Summary: Torrential rain triggered fresh landslides across J&K on Friday, prompting authorities to keep Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) closed for traffic. More than 1,000 vehicles remained stranded at Ramban, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, Lakhanpur and Samba due to the closure.

Article Title: Haryana’s air pollution action plan: Centre suggests strict enforcement and accelerated implementation to curb pollution in a time-bound manner
Article Text:
Centre reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Friday reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution in Delhi-NCR, and emphasised the need for “accelerated implementation, stronger inter-agency coordination and strict enforcement” to ensure substantial reduction in pollution before the onset of the winter season when stubble burning and meteorological conditions raise the levels of pollutants.The meeting, chaired by Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in Gurugram, held extensive discussions on Haryana’s air pollution action plan and multiple steps, which are being taken, with particular focus on legacy waste, road dust, industrial pollution and strengthening the infrastructure to enable accelerated EV adoption.Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and senior officials of the state govt attended the meeting."The window before the winter season must be fully utilized to implement pollution control measures in mission mode. Timely execution, effective coordination and strict enforcement will be critical to achieving visible improvements in Delhi-NCR's air quality,” said Yadav while emphasising the urgency of timely action.On critical issue of stubble burning that increases level of air pollutants in Delhi-NCR during every winter, Yadav urged the state govt to bridge gaps in procurement of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery and accelerate establishment of Custom Hiring Centres.He also emphasised the need for intensive Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns and farmer training programmes to promote effective use of CRM equipment. He suggested that local elected representatives identify stubble-burning hotspots in coordination with Gram Panchayats, and asked District Collectors to survey industrial units and document their crop residue storage and consumption capacities to facilitate efficient demand-supply management.“The state authorities were also advised to ensure adequate availability of crop residue balers,” said a statement from the environment ministry on the review meeting.It said, “The minister also reviewed progress on construction and demolition waste management and requested that the establishment of Secondary Collection Centres for C&D waste be expedited. He also stressed that liquidation of legacy waste should be undertaken on a war footing.”Referring to municipal solid waste (MSW) and biomass burning, Yadav called for the constitution of dedicated task forces and emphasized achieving 100% collection of municipal solid waste and biomass to eliminate littering and prevent open burning.On the issue of End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, Yadav requested the authorities to expedite issuance of No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for transfer of eligible EoL vehicles outside the NCR, while simultaneously encouraging scientific scrapping of old and unfit vehicles. He also called for faster replacement of old polluting vehicles with electric vehicles under the ‘Parivartan’ scheme.“The minister requested that Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras be installed at all fuel stations for effective implementation of the ‘No PUCC, No Fuel’ initiative. Stressing the need to improve urban traffic management, Yadav asked the authorities to identify traffic congestion hotspots on a mission mode and implement suitable mitigation measures at the earliest,” said the official statement.Reviewing industrial pollution control measures, Yadav stressed the need for accelerated installation of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) across industrial units.
Article Summary: The Centre on Friday reviewed measures taken by the Haryana govt to address the issue of air pollution in Delhi-NCR. The meeting, chaired by Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in Gurugram, held extensive discussions on air pollution action plan.

Article Title: Fast-track special courts slow as backlog mounts; nearly 2.5 lakh cases pending
Article Text:
Fast-track special courts slow as backlog mounts; nearly 2.5 lakh cases pending

BENGALURU: At a time when Centre has announced setting up of Fast-Track Courts (FTC) to ensure expeditious trials in paper leak cases in the wake of the 2026 NEET fiasco, the country’s Fast-Track Special Courts (FTSCs) — operating under the most recent scheme introduced in Oct 2019 — are buckling under mounting backlogs.Govt data analysed by TOI shows that annual disposals by FTSCs, created to deliver swift justice in some of the most sensitive criminal cases (rape and Pocso), dropped to 66,500 cases in 2025, down from a record 85,595 in 2024, a decline of more than 22%. At the same time, pending cases rose from a little more than 2 lakh at the end of 2024 to nearly 2.5 lakh by the close of 2025.The trend suggests that despite expanding judicial capacity, fresh cases continue to outnumber disposals. Since 2021, pendency has increased by nearly one-third, from around 1.8 lakh to nearly 2.5 lakh , even as annual disposals almost doubled between 2021 and 2024 before falling last year.The figures point to a structural challenge rather than a temporary slowdown. Fast-track courts were conceived to shorten the time victims wait for justice, but rising case inflows, judicial vacancies, infrastructure constraints and limited courtroom capacity have continued to push pendency upwards.The result is that courts designed to accelerate trials are themselves carrying growing backlogs.As per the latest information from the govt, the FTSC scheme currently operates 775 courts, including 398 exclusive POCSO courts, across the country. This is against a target of at least 790 courts that should have been functional. The courts have disposed of nearly 3.9 lakh cases since inception. Yet with nearly 2.5 lakh cases still pending, the gains have not translated into a sustained reduction in backlog.The experience varies widely across States. While some States have managed comparatively low pendency per court, others continue to operate under far heavier workloads, indicating that the effectiveness of the scheme depends not only on the number of courts but also on staffing, infrastructure and the volume of new cases entering the system.The latest figures relate specifically to Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), which are a separate scheme launched by the Centre in Oct 2019 to hear rape and Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cases, which has since been extended up to Sept 30, 2026. These should not be confused with the original Fast Track Courts (FTCs), which were introduced nearly two decades earlier — 880 of which are functional currently.These courts had disposed of more than 13 lakh cases in 2025, up from 11.7 lakh in 2024, but lower than 15.2 lakh in 2023. However, year-wise pendency data on FTCs wasn’t immediately available. The department of justice’s dashboard, which was accessible as of July 23 night, was offline on Friday.History Of Fast-Track CourtsIndia’s first FTCs were established in 2000 following the recommendations of the 11th Finance Commission. The idea was to create additional courts on a temporary basis to clear long-pending sessions cases and reduce the number of undertrial prisoners.The Centre funded the scheme until March 31, 2011, after which States were expected to use their own resources. While several States retained or expanded FTCs, others allowed them to lapse, leading to wide variations across the country.The policy then evolved after the 2012 Nirbhaya case, as public pressure mounted for quicker trials in sexual offence cases. The 14th Finance Commission later supported the creation of 1,800 Fast Track Courts using the increased fiscal space available to States, though without dedicated central funding.And, in Oct 2019 the FTSCs scheme under the Nirbhaya Fund was launched. Since then, the ordinary FTCs remain the responsibility of state govts and high courts, while the Centre funds only the FTSC scheme.
Article Summary: Fast-track courts were conceived to shorten the time victims wait for justice. Rising case inflows, judicial vacancies, infrastructure constraints and limited courtroom capacity have continued to push pendency upwards. The result is that courts designed to accelerate trials are themselves carrying growing backlogs.

Article Title: Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident
Article Text:
Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday condemned the attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping 'unacceptable' and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and global trade.The incident took place on July 18, when the MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. According to the MEA, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. One Indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two Indians are reported to be safe.In a statement, the MEA said, "On 18 July 2026, the commercial vessel MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. At the time of the incident, there were ten crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. As per available information, one Indian national tragically lost his life in the attack. We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved family of the deceased. The other two Indian nationals on board are reported to be safe."Condemning the attack, the ministry said, "India unequivocally condemns such attacks targeting commercial shipping and placing the lives of innocent civilian crew members at risk.It is a matter of serious concern that the freedom of navigation and international commerce is facing increasing threats. India calls upon all concerned parties to uphold international obligations to ensure the safety and security of maritime navigation and uninterrupted flow of global commerce. "The latest attack comes after MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo vessel, was struck shortly after departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on July 19. The vessel had 17 crew members, including five Indian nationals. Four Indians were killed and one was critically injured in that attack.The MEA had then condemned the strike, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted, while assuring that India's mission in Ukraine was extending all possible assistance to those affected.The back-to-back attacks have heightened concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea, where renewed hostilities have increased risks to civilian vessels and global maritime trade.
Article Summary: The incident took place on July 18, when the MV OMORFI was attacked. According to the MEA, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. One Indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two Indians are reported to be safe.

Article Title: Three chemical parks to be set up under BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Union Cabinet on Friday approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA-Rasayan) scheme for establishing three dedicated chemical parks in the country.The scheme will have a total financial outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, of which Rs 3,000 crore will be used for establishing common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities inside the parks, while the remaining Rs 30 crore has been earmarked for administrative expenditure.Announced in the Union Budget, the scheme will run for five years. While the Centre will provide a grant of up to Rs 1,000 crore for each park, the state where it is established will have to contribute at least Rs 500 crore.Govt said the BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme is expected to promote the development of the chemical industry and its value chain, including upstream, downstream and ancillary industries, while ensuring efficient utilisation of resources.By providing shared common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities tailored to the needs of the chemical industry, the scheme is expected to enhance cost competitiveness and make the Indian chemical industry globally competitive. It will also help the sector integrate better with global value chains, boosting exports and import substitution.The scheme will create an environment-friendly ecosystem with centralised facilities such as a common effluent treatment plant, treatment, storage and disposal facilities, and hazardous waste management infrastructure. Govt said the development of the chemical sector will generate employment and contribute to economic growth.
Article Summary: The scheme will have a total financial outlay of Rs 3,030 crore. The Centre will provide a grant of up to Rs 1,000 crore for each park. The state where it is established will have to contribute at least Rs 500 crore.

Article Title: Government pushes competition in power distribution
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: Union power ministry’s consultative committee met on Thursday to discuss a consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing that would allow multiple electricity suppliers to use the same distribution network.The proposed reform aims to improve service quality, encourage competition, reduce infrastructure duplication and give consumers the freedom to choose their electricity provider.The draft National Electricity Policy-2026, which is under consultation and is likely to be placed before the cabinet soon, has also underlined the need to phase out monopoly in electricity distribution and introduce competition by allowing multiple players.According to officials, the existing legal framework permits more than one distribution licensee in the same area, but requires each of them to establish its own distribution network. This results in duplication of infrastructure, higher capital expenditure, discourages fresh investment and leads to “inefficient utilisation of resources”.Mumbai is the only city where consumers have exercised supplier choice for several years, while the distribution network is developed in a coordinated manner under the supervision of the state electricity regulatory commission.Emphasising the consumer-centric nature of the reform, Union power minister Manohar Lal said consumers would have the freedom to choose their electricity supplier, similar to the choices available today in sectors such as telecom and aviation. "Increased competition is expected to encourage better consumer service, improved reliability, greater innovation and operational efficiency, while ensuring optimal utilisation of existing infrastructure and avoiding unnecessary expenditure," the minister said at the meeting.Power ministry, in a statement, said members of Parliament who are part of the consultative committee offered valuable suggestions on the proposed framework. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks."New distribution licensees will be able to use the existing network by paying regulated wheeling charges, while retaining the option to develop their own network wherever permitted by the concerned state electricity regulatory commission," govt said in the statement.
Article Summary: Proposed reform aims to improve service quality, encourage competition, reduce infrastructure duplication and give consumers the freedom to choose their electricity provider. Draft National Electricity Policy-2026 is under consultation and is likely to be placed before the cabinet soon. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks.

Article Title: Creation and nurturing of society impossible without motherhood: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addresses valedictory session of a two-day national meeting on 'Contemporary Motherhood' organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha.

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Friday said motherhood is the foundation of creation, nurturing and continuity of society, asserting that "the creation, nurturing and sustenance of the world are impossible without motherhood. "Addressing the valedictory session of a two-day national meeting on "Contemporary Motherhood" organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha at the Ambedkar International Centre, Bhagwat said the core principles of motherhood remain timeless even as society changes.He described mothers as a child's first teacher and the primary source of emotional support throughout life, saying they play a decisive role in shaping values and giving the right direction to a person's thinking.Bhagwat said parents should spend more time with their families and maintain open communication with children. He stressed that children learn more through observation than instruction, making it important for parents to lead by example. He also said parents should continue to expand their own knowledge so they can address their children's questions and curiosity.The RSS chief said many debates in society stem from misconceptions, some of which are deliberately created.Referring to Indian culture, he said it had long been portrayed as flawed despite having a strong civilisational foundation. He urged people to move forward with confidence in India's history, traditions and knowledge systems.He also said unity amid diversity lies at the heart of Indian culture and called for strengthening families and social institutions by following Indian cultural values rather than adopting foreign lifestyles without reflection.Bhagwat began his address by saying it was somewhat paradoxical for him to speak on motherhood, adding that women have the primary authority to speak on the subject. He said the organisation had already held extensive discussions on the theme and noted that thinkers such as Swami Vivekananda, Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore had reflected extensively on motherhood and its relevance to society.The event was organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha, a women's organisation that says it works towards "nation-building through motherhood." The two-day meeting, held on July 23 and 24, brought together around 280 women from different states to discuss the role of motherhood in the context of changing social conditions and the Indian family system.According to the organisers, more than 900 women attended the concluding session, while between 2,000 and 2,500 women had registered for the dialogue on the theme. The organisation said it held conventions across 23 regions in India in 2026, involving around 37,000 women, and is currently active in 33 regions with nearly six lakh women associated with its activities. It also has a presence in 14 countries, including the United States and the Netherlands.
Article Summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat said motherhood is the foundation of creation, nurturing and continuity of society. He was addressing the valedictory session of a two-day national meeting on "Contemporary Motherhood" organised by Vishwa Mangalya Sabha.

Article Title: NTA terminates 47 officials, begins specialist-led rebuild
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: The National Testing Agency has terminated 47 officials and begun rebuilding its workforce with specialist leadership in cybersecurity, forensic investigation, test-centre operations and assessment research, government sources said on Friday.Some of those terminated will also face legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies. More measures are expected as responsibility is fixed for failures in national entrance examinations.The first phase includes four General Manager appointments and 16 Young Professionals through UPSC’s PRATIBHA Setu portal. Recruitment will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting on Saturday, July 25, ministry sources said.The crackdown follows the NEET-UG paper leak, which forced nearly 20 lakh candidates to take the examination again on June 21 after the May 3 test was cancelled. Sources stressed that the 47 personnel had been terminated, not merely transferred or marked for removal. Their names, ranks and alleged roles were not disclosed. Cases indicating criminal wrongdoing will be referred to the appropriate agencies, while departmental and legal proceedings will follow separately.The four General Managers will be appointed on three-year contracts.The assessment and psychometrics head will oversee question banks, normalisation, equating and calibration, and pilots on computer-adaptive testing and AI-assisted assessment.The test-centre operations head will supervise NTA ’s network across more than 500 cities and select overseas centres, including empanelment, capacity, accessibility, amenities, examination-day operations and coordination with administrations.The information-security head will serve as Chief Information Security Officer, responsible for systems, networks, applications, candidate data, a round-the-clock Security Operations Centre and compliance with data-protection, information-technology and CERT-In requirements.The vigilance, investigation and forensics head will lead malpractice inquiries, build in-house digital-forensics capability and coordinate with the CBI, Intelligence Bureau, Enforcement Directorate, state police and cybercrime units under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.NTA will also engage 16 Young Professionals through PRATIBHA Setu — Professional Resource And Talent Integration Bridge for Hiring Aspirants — for the first time. The platform gives verified employers access to willing candidates who cleared stages of UPSC examinations but were not recommended in the final merit list.Twelve positions will be in academic research, two in legal research and two in finance and accounts. Appointments will initially be for 24 months, extendable to 36 months based on performance.The changes seek to reduce NTA’s dependence on temporary manpower. It has 39 sanctioned permanent posts, all on deputation, but only 24 are filled, against 73 contractual personnel and 124 outsourced workers.Further hiring will follow across 10 functional verticals recommended by the Radhakrishnan committee. NTA has also initiated fresh empanelment of subject experts and translators.The overhaul will accompany changes to examination delivery. NEET-UG will shift from OMR-based testing to computer-based testing from 2027, bringing it closer to JEE Main and CUET. The move should reduce physical movement of papers, enable multiple question sets and create a digital trail, but will require secure centres, stronger cybersecurity and safeguards against technical failures.The government is also reviewing outsourcing in registration, centre management, technology services and handling of confidential material. The new model will define responsibility, strengthen audits and background checks, reduce agencies handling sensitive information and impose tougher penalties for security failures.Sources said the reset would combine accountability for past lapses with safeguards against future leaks and malpractice.
Article Summary: The first phase includes four General Manager appointments and 16 Young Professionals through UPSC’s PRATIBHA Setu portal. Recruitment will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which will hold its first meeting on Saturday, July 25.

Article Title: RSS women's wing kicks off three-day national meet in Haryana
Article Text:
The meeting commenced with the lighting of a ceremonial lamp, followed by tributes to the organisation's former office-bearers

Organisational review and expansion

Highlights of recent activities

NEW DELHI: The Rashtriya Sevika Samiti, the women's organisation ideologically affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ), on Friday began its three-day first half-yearly national executive and representatives' meeting at the Madhav Smriti campus in Samalkha, Haryana.Around 500 representatives from 38 provinces are expected to participate in the meeting, which will continue until July 26. The meeting is being attended by Pramukh Sanchalika Shantakkaji and Pramukh Karyavahika Sita Gayatri.The meeting commenced with the lighting of a ceremonial lamp, followed by tributes to the organisation's former office-bearers Rukmini Akka and Rekhatai Raje.Representatives also paid homage to other deceased workers, noted personalities including Asha Bhosle, Suman Kalyanpur and S. Janaki, as well as victims of terrorist attacks, natural disasters and accidents.Addressing the inaugural session, Pramukh Karyavahika Sita Gayatri said the organisation should continue its efforts towards women's empowerment while contributing to nation-building. Referring to the birth anniversary of the organisation's founder Lakshmibai Kelkar, observed as Sankalp Diwas, she called upon members to carry forward the work of the organisation.Sita Gayatri also referred to recent developments, including India's humanitarian medical assistance to Iran, describing it as an example of the country's outreach.She also mentioned India's performance at the International Chemistry Olympiad and the ICC Women's T20 World Cup as indicators of the country's achievements in different fields.The organisation reviewed its activities over the past year, stating that it has expanded its network of branches, meeting centres and service projects.It is currently running service activities at 2,866 locations across the country.These initiatives include projects related to education, value-based learning, self-reliance, healthcare and yoga centres. The organisation also said it operates hostels for girls from remote areas.Around 250 training camps were organised across the country in 2026, in which nearly 15,241 women volunteers received training.The organisation also highlighted several initiatives undertaken during the year. It said volunteers organised a route march in West Bengal after a long gap and referred to a training camp in Jammu where participants continued activities despite heavy rain and strong winds.During a visit to Chhattisgarh, the organisation's chief interacted with women from around 25 different communities as part of a social harmony initiative.It also highlighted the 'Nari Se Narayani' conference organised jointly with the Bharatiya Vidvat Parishad at Vigyan Bhavan in Delhi on International Women's Day.The event was attended by over 1,500 women from across the country, with President Droupadi Murmu addressing the concluding session.The three-day meeting is scheduled to conclude on July 26.
Article Summary: Rashtriya Sevika Samiti is ideologically affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Around 500 representatives from 38 provinces are expected to participate in the meeting. The organisation reviewed its activities over the past year, stating that it has expanded its network.

Article Title: PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video amid NEET protest
Article Text:
PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi gained around 1 million Instagram followers overnight after he released his selfie video on Thursday night addressing concerns of the NEET paper leak.Currently PM Modi has 102 million followers on Instagram. His video captioned: "More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow’s Cabinet!" has garnered 271 million views so far along with 15 million likes and 1.3 million comments on Instagram.In the video, he announced that the government would introduce tougher measures to tackle examination paper leaks. He also informed about the Union Cabinet meeting agenda held on Friday."I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakh of students and their guardians," he said."Numerous effective measures have been taken in the past two and a half months since the paper leak incident. The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our most important responsibility was to ensure that students' year is not wasted. The government used all its might to ensure that 22 lakh students could take their exams in the shortest possible time," he added.The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared amendments to the anti-paper leak law, proposing stricter punishment for those involved in examination paper leaks. Sources said the revised law prescribes up to 10 years in prison and a fine of as much as Rs 10 crore, while raising the minimum jail term from three years to five years.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video. His video captioned: "More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow’s Cabinet!" has garnered 271 million views so far along with 15 million likes and 1.3 million comments on Instagram.
